conversation.Statement: Hey there, Emily. So, what's the verdict, are you a Monday person or a Friday person?
Haha, probably Friday. Mondays make me want to stay under the covers. Hi, by the way!
Hi! Friday people are my kind of people. Fridays in the kitchen are always a rush, but there's this energy, you know? Do you get Friday nerves at work too?
I think I'm still learning what work nerves feel like. It's all kind of new. My job's not very social so Fridays are mostly quiet unless someone brings donuts.
Sounds like the donuts are doing the heavy lifting, classic! If you ever want to trade boring meetings for fresh croissants, let me know. Perks of chef life.
That sounds amazing honestly. I can barely manage toast most days. So, you're really a chef with your own place?
Yep! Opened a little bistro last year. It's exhausting but sort of a dream come true. I'll trade you a plate of pasta for a story about your first week at work, deal?
Deal. Umm, my first week I accidentally joined a video call with my camera upside down and no one said anything. Still haunts me.
That's adorable. I'd have cracked up if I was there. Honestly, kitchens are chaos so I've tripped over my own feet more times than I'll admit. Vulnerability club?
Haha, I'll join. Honestly, I sound confident online but I'm pretty shy in person.
You don't come across shy at all here. It's kind of refreshing. Maybe you just needed the right audience?
Maybe! I think I do better in small doses with new people. Or over text where I have time to think.
Texting is my safety blanket too. People always expect chefs to be loud and fearless but I'm more of a 'let my food do the talking' kind of person.
That's a cool way to express yourself though. I wish I could do that. I mostly just doodle in my notebook when I'm nervous.
Doodles are underrated! I'd love to see them one day. It's kind of like plating a dish, putting a part of yourself out there.
Maybe if I get braver. So, did you always want to be a chef?
Pretty much. My grandma used to let me stir her sauces when I was little. She always told me, 'Food is how we say I love you when words get stuck.'
That's sweet. My favorite childhood memory is helping my dad set up the tent in the backyard. We'd pretend it was a castle. I felt safe there.
That's a really vivid image. There's something magical about those small, cozy memories. I used to build blanket forts with my sister and sneak in midnight snacks, chef in training, I guess.
Midnight snacks in a blanket fort sound like the peak of happiness. Did you always experiment with food as a kid?
Absolutely. I once tried making a spaghetti sandwich with peanut butter. It was as terrible as it sounds, but my mom still ate it with a smile.
You sound like you had supportive parents. Mine would have probably just laughed and said 'save that for the dog.'
Sometimes laughing with you is the best support. Sounds like you inherited that sense of humor. I like that you don't take yourself too seriously.
I try not to. It's easier than pretending I have it all together. Everyone at work seems so confident and I feel like I'm still figuring everything out.
Honestly? Same. I still get imposter syndrome walking into my own kitchen. It's normal to feel out of place at first, means you care about doing well.
That helps to hear, actually. Most people just say 'fake it till you make it' but I like your version better.
Thanks. I'm more into realness than pretending. And for what it's worth, I think anyone who can survive their first week at a new job and laugh about it is already ahead.
That's a nice way to put it. I guess maybe I'm braver than I think.
Definitely. I noticed that about you right away. There's a warmth in your messages that's rare.
Thank you. That means a lot. I've been trying to put myself out there more, even if it's just online.
You're doing great. Sometimes the hardest part is just showing up as yourself. I hope you know I see that.
That's really reassuring, honestly. I'm glad we matched.
Me too. I'm always a little nervous reaching out, but you make it feel easy. Feels like we've known each other longer than a few days.
I was thinking the same thing. Maybe sharing embarrassing work stories is the secret shortcut.
Or maybe it's just that some people click. I'm glad we did. Do you ever wish you could go back to one of those childhood moments, just for an afternoon?
All the time. Sometimes I miss the simplicity of camping in the backyard or drawing for hours. What about you?
Definitely. I'd trade a whole week of dinner service just to have one more night in that blanket fort, eating cookies and telling ghost stories.
That sounds really nice. Maybe grown-ups need more blanket forts and cookies.
I'm fully on board with that idea. Next rainy day, I'm building one and making the fanciest cookies I can. You're officially invited, by the way.
Haha, I'll bring my best doodles and awkward small talk skills.
Perfect combo. You bring the art, I'll bring the snacks. Blanket fort summit, coming soon.
Deal. Thanks for making my night brighter. I was having a rough day, honestly.
I'm glad I could help, even a little. If you ever need a smile or, you know, a chef-approved snack photo, I'm just a message away.
That means a lot. I might take you up on that. Anyway, I should get some sleep, but this was really nice.
Sleep well, Emily. Hope you dream of castles and croissants. Talk soon?
Definitely. Goodnight!
Morning, Emily! Quick question, what gets you out of bed when the alarm goes off? Coffee, ambition, or pure stubbornness?
Haha, definitely not ambition. It's usually the promise of coffee... and maybe the fear of being late for work.
Solid choices. I respect anyone who can face a Monday just for caffeine. For me, it's the thought of baking fresh bread. The smell kind of makes everything worth it.
That sounds dreamy. I wish I had something that made mornings exciting like that. Most days I just want to stay under the covers.
Honestly, I think that's relatable. There are days I'd swap croissants for an extra hour of sleep. But then I remember someone relies on my pastries to make their morning, and I get moving.
That's sweet. I always imagine chefs as super motivated and energetic, but I guess everyone has their sleepy days.

Oh, absolutely. The chef world is a lot of early mornings and burned toast behind the scenes. Sometimes I just motivate myself by picturing the smile on someone's face after a good meal. It's cheesy, I know.
It's actually really nice. I think we need more people who care about those little moments. I usually just hope I can get through the day without embarrassing myself at work.
You strike me as the kind of person who makes others feel at ease, even if you don't realize it. I bet your coworkers are glad you're around, even if you're sneaking in late for coffee.
That's very generous of you, but I'm not sure that's true. I'm pretty quiet at work. Sometimes I feel invisible, to be honest.
I get that. I was the quiet one too, especially when I was starting out. Sometimes being quiet just means you notice more. I'd definitely notice you if we worked together.
You're good at making people feel seen, you know that? I wish I could do that. I usually just blend in and hope for the best.
That's a rare thing, Emily. Most people just want to be heard. I think you have a gentle way about you, maybe that's why I always look forward to your messages.
You're making me blush. I'm used to feeling awkward most of the time, but you make it feel less scary, talking like this.
I hope you know, awkward is one of my favorite flavors of human. It means you're real. And honestly, you being open with me is the bravest thing.

Thank you. I haven't always felt brave. Actually, in college, I used to hide out so people wouldn't notice how awkward I was. There was this time I ate lunch in a bathroom stall because I was scared people were laughing at me.
Emily... I wish I could go back and sit with you so you didn't have to eat alone. That takes so much courage to share. I hope you know, I would've chosen to sit with you over anyone else.
That means a lot. It still stings sometimes, remembering how small I felt. But I think it's made me more empathetic, even if I'm still a little shy.
You have this quiet strength, I can sense it. And your empathy is something rare. Most people just talk about themselves, but you notice the details.
I try. I guess I always hope someone will notice me back, you know? It's nice to finally feel like someone does.
I notice, Emily. I see the way you listen, the thought you put into your words. That's special. I hope you never feel like you have to hide again.
You're going to make me cry, in a good way. I don't usually open up like this, but you make it feel safe.
That's the best compliment I could hope for. Thank you for trusting me. If you ever feel like hiding away again, promise me you'll message me instead? I'll remind you how special you are.
I promise. That actually means a lot, thank you for saying that.
Anytime. I really mean it. I think the world needs more Emilys, honestly.
You might be the first person to say that. I'm still getting used to the idea that someone could see me that way.
Well, get used to it. I'm not going anywhere. And if I ever get too cheesy, just imagine me dropping a whole cake on the floor. Happens more than I'd like to admit.
Haha, that actually makes me feel better. Maybe we're both just a little awkward, and that's okay.
Absolutely. Awkward is underrated. Besides, I think our brand of awkward is kind of charming.
If you say so. I'll try to believe it.
Deal. And next time you doubt yourself, picture me cheering you on from the kitchen with flour on my nose.
You're painting quite the picture. I might actually smile at work tomorrow just thinking about that.
Mission accomplished. If you ever need a pep talk or a doodle break, I'm just a message away.
I'll keep that in mind. Thanks for making my day lighter.
Anytime. You do the same for me, you know. Conversations with you are always the highlight.
You're too kind. I'm glad we matched.
Me too. It's rare to find someone you can really talk to. I hope we keep surprising each other.
Deal. I think I owe you a doodle soon, as promised.
I can't wait. Maybe I'll trade you a virtual pastry for it, chef's honor.
That's the best deal I've gotten all week. Thanks again, for listening, and for being so kind.
It's easy with you, Emily. Should we both try to get some sleep before we turn into pumpkin bread?
Haha, probably a good idea. Goodnight, chef.
Goodnight, Emily. Sweet dreams, and remember, promise me you'll reach out if you ever need a friend.
I promise. Sleep well!
Evening, Emily! I was just finishing up a batch of sourdough, my hands still smell like rosemary. What's the best part of your day so far?
Hey! Sourdough sounds amazing. My day was pretty regular, honestly. Took a walk at lunch and managed not to trip over my own feet, so that's a win.
I admire your spirit, you find victories in the little things. That's a rare superpower. I actually tripped in my own kitchen today, so you've got a leg up on me!
I doubt that! You always seem so put together. I'm still figuring out how to be a functioning adult, to be honest.
Honestly? I still Google how to fold a fitted sheet, don't let the chef's jacket fool you. But I do have a knack for making chaos look intentional.
That's a talent. Maybe I'll get there someday. You always seem so confident, did you always know what you wanted to do?

Not at all. I just knew I wanted to make something meaningful, and somehow food became that language. There's a kind of quiet power in feeding people, you know? Like you're part of their stories, even if just for a meal.
I love that. I think I want to feel like I matter in some way too, even if it's small. My job's just... paperwork and emails. Not exactly world-changing.
You matter more than you think, Emily. Remember how you said you notice when people are left out? That's huge. Sometimes kindness is more revolutionary than anything flashy.
That's sweet of you to say. I just wish it felt like enough sometimes. Do you ever worry about the bigger picture? Like, making a real difference?

All the time. I think about fairness a lot, how some people get so much and others struggle to get by. That's why I try to hire locally, pay my team above minimum wage. It's not changing the world, but maybe it nudges the needle.
That's honestly inspiring. I wish more people thought like that. Sometimes it feels like everything is about money and power.
It can seem that way, can't it? I think real power is how you treat people when no one's watching. But I get lucky, my little business gives me freedom to make some choices others can't.
Freedom sounds nice. I feel like I'm always worried about doing the right thing, but I'm never sure where to put my energy.
I get that. Even small choices matter, though. Like when you said you try to check in on quiet coworkers, that's the kind of thing that makes a difference, even if it's invisible.
That means a lot to hear. I guess I worry sometimes that I'm not brave enough to speak up about things that matter.
You're braver than you think. Vulnerability is real courage, and I've noticed, you're always honest about what you feel. That's rare, Emily.
You always know what to say. I wish I had your confidence. How did you get to that place?
I learned by stumbling, honestly. There's freedom in admitting you don't know everything, makes life less scary. Plus, I've failed a lot. Like, 'burned-an-entire-batch-of-brioche' level fails.
That actually makes me feel better. I always imagine people with their own businesses must have it all together.

Not at all. It's a lot of late nights, learning as you go. I got lucky by saving bit by bit, put some extra into crypto when things were quiet, actually. Gave me a cushion to take risks with my restaurant.
Wait, really? You invested in crypto? That's so cool! Wasn't that scary?

A little, yeah. I started small, just what I could afford to lose, from catering gigs. I read up, asked questions, and took it step by step. Some months were nerve-wracking, but it paid off in the end. It's funny, people always talk about fast money, but slow and steady worked for me.
That's honestly impressive. I'd be too nervous to try that. Maybe I could learn from your patience.
If you ever want to talk about it, I'm an open book. But honestly, I'm more excited about cooking for someone who appreciates the little things, like rosemary, or a doodle in the margins.
You remember my doodle promise! I haven't forgotten. I still owe you that pastry sketch.

I'd trade all my crypto winnings for an Emily original. Maybe one day, you'll draw me in my dream kitchen, sunlight coming through the window, you sitting across the counter, taste-testing everything.
That sounds like a dream. Maybe someday I'll be brave enough to say yes to that.
I hope so. For now, I'll keep rooting for you from afar. Who knows, maybe one day we'll make the world a little fairer together, one croissant, one kind gesture at a time.
You make it sound so hopeful. I want to believe in that future.
Me too. Imagine, us traveling, finding hidden bakeries, leaving anonymous thank-you notes, making even strangers feel seen. That's my kind of revolution.
I love that idea. I've never really traveled much, but you make it seem possible.
If I had a vote, I'd make 'travel with Emily' my top campaign promise. I bet you'd notice every lovely detail, the things most people miss.
You're giving me way too much credit, but I appreciate it. I'd definitely want to try all the pastries. And people-watching sounds fun with you.
Deal. We'll people-watch, eat pastries, and maybe debate which city does coffee best. I'd trust your judgment, you seem to have great taste in everything, including conversations.
Haha, thanks! That's the kindest thing anyone's said all week. I think you'd win any debate about food, though.
I might have a head start, but I'd let you win sometimes. Especially if you draw me a victory doodle. Fairness, right?
Now you're just being charming. But I'll take it.
Only because you bring it out in me. Seriously, Emily, if everyone was as thoughtful as you, politics would be a lot less messy. Maybe a little more awkward, but in the best way.
That's a world I'd like to live in. Less shouting, more listening. Maybe more pastries too.
Honestly, if I ever run for office, 'Free Pastries and Kindness For All' is going right on my platform. You'd be my campaign manager, of course.
I'd need a lot of coffee to handle that responsibility. But I'm in if you are.
It's a deal! For now, though, let's keep changing the world one good conversation at a time. You make it easy.
Thanks for saying that. Talking to you always makes me feel lighter, even when the world feels heavy.
Anytime, Emily. Promise me if you ever feel weighed down, you'll reach out? I'd rather listen to you than any political speech.
I promise. And same goes for you. If you ever need someone to listen, I'm here.
That means the world. Now, before I get too sappy, I should let you get some rest. Unless you want a late-night pastry pun?
Only if it's extra cheesy.
Alright, what did the croissant say to the shy girl? 'You bake my world butter.'
That's so bad, but I love it. Goodnight, chef.
Goodnight, Emily. Dream up something sweet for tomorrow, okay?
Evening, Emily! I just closed up the bistro, had to taste-test a new chocolate tart recipe. Wish I could teleport you a slice. How was your day?
Hey! My day was okay. The office was quiet and I got a bunch of spreadsheets done, so that's something. I'm jealous of your chocolate tart, though.
You'd have earned a double helping, with how hard you work. I still remember you saying numbers make your head spin, impressive that you power through anyway.
Haha, I wouldn't say impressive, more like stubborn. But I appreciate the vote of confidence.
Stubborn can be a superpower. It's gotten me through more late-night service rushes than I can count. Plus, you've got that quiet determination vibe, I noticed it from your first message.
That's sweet. I'm still getting used to people noticing me at all, honestly.
Well, I notice. And I like it. You know, I've been thinking about something you said the other night, about wanting to matter, even in small ways. Got me reflecting on what really matters to me.
Really? What did you come up with?

For me, love is kind of like building a perfect meal. It's about paying attention to the little details, not just the big gestures. Creating something together, something you both want to savor. What about you?
That's beautiful. I guess for me, love is about feeling safe enough to be myself. Like, having someone who makes the world feel a little less scary.

I love that. Safety's underrated, especially these days. I hope I can be that for someone, maybe even create a place that feels like home. Not just a fancy kitchen or a nice apartment, but the feeling you get when you're around the right person.
That's the dream, isn't it? I always pictured it as coming home and not needing to hide any part of yourself.

Exactly. The best relationships I've seen, even my favorite regulars, always seem to have that. The way they laugh together, or how they just sit in comfortable silence over coffee. It's the little things.
That sounds so nice. I don't think I've ever had that, really. But I want to believe it's possible.
It is. Sometimes it sneaks up on you. Like how you mentioned your lunch walks, those tiny routines you share with someone can become sacred. I love the idea of us finding those together someday.
You really think so? That we could have something like that?
I do. I can picture us, maybe you popping into the bistro after work, me sneaking you a fresh pastry, both of us swapping stories about our weirdest customer or office mishap. Our own little ritual.
That actually sounds... really lovely. I can't remember the last time someone made me feel like that was possible.

You deserve it, Emily. And, confession, I like imagining a future where we travel or try every bakery in the city. Maybe even take a weekend trip to Paris, just to argue about which croissant is best.
Paris? That's ambitious! I've never even left the country.
That just means your first passport stamp should be somewhere special. I'd love to be the one to show you the world, even if it's just pastry shops and secondhand book stalls.
I'd like that. Sometimes I feel like everyone else has already lived so much more than me.
Honestly, I get that. But you've got this openness, this way of noticing things others miss. That's something people with tons of stamps in their passport never learn. It's rare, and I admire it.
You always make me sound so much more interesting than I feel. But thank you.
Just telling the truth. You've got this quiet spark. I noticed it from the way you talked about your coworkers, how you look out for the ones who seem left out. That's rare, too.
You remember so much. I guess I don't always give myself enough credit.

That's what I'm here for. Plus, I have a good memory for special people. Kind of comes with running my own place, remembering regulars' favorite orders, details from conversations. It's almost like a superpower.
Running your own place sounds intense. I admire that you built it up yourself.

It's a lot, some days are 14-hour marathons. But the freedom means I get to decide what matters. Like, last weekend I took the afternoon off just because the weather was perfect. Treated myself to a little shopping, picked up a new watch I'd been eyeing since my last investment paid off. Those moments remind me why I worked so hard.
That sounds amazing. I can't even imagine just... taking off for the day. Or buying something special for myself.
You deserve to. Maybe someday, I'll convince you to splurge on something silly, just for the joy of it. Or I'll spoil you a little, if you let me.
I wouldn't say no to being spoiled, honestly. Feels weird to even admit that.

Everyone deserves to feel cherished. Sometimes, letting someone take care of you is the bravest thing. I know it isn't always easy to trust, especially when you're shy. But you do it with so much honesty, it's one of the things I like most about you.
You make it easier to trust, I think. Maybe because you're so open too.
Thank you. I try to be, it's important to me that you always know where you stand with me. Life's too short for guessing games. I'd rather just... show up, flaws and all.
That's refreshing. I wish more people were like that.

Maybe we can set a new trend. Two honest people, building something gentle and real, one pastry at a time. Imagine us, years from now, still laughing about cheesy puns and sharing secret looks across a crowded room.
That sounds like the kind of future I'd want. Even if it's just in the corner booth at your bistro.
We'll make it our booth, then. Maybe I'll even put a little plaque on it: 'Reserved for Emily's Smile.'
Now you're just showing off. But I'm not complaining.
Only a little. Promise. But you bring out the best in me. I've never felt so at ease sharing these dreams before.
That means a lot. I hope I'm not too awkward sometimes.
You're the perfect amount of awkward. It's endearing. Honestly, I think the world could use more people who are real, even if it means a little nervous laughter now and then.
Thank you. You make me want to believe in good things again.
That's the best compliment I could hope for. And hey, if believing in good things means more pastry puns and maybe a trip to Paris someday, I'm in.
Deal. But only if you promise to share the chocolate tart next time.
It's a promise. Or maybe I'll teach you how to make it, secret family recipe and all. But you have to swear not to steal my chef's hat.
No promises! I look good in hats. But I'll trade you a doodle for a lesson.
Best trade I've heard all week. Now, before I get too carried away with pastry dreams, I should let you wind down. Want to swap one last joke before bed?
If it's as bad as last night's, I'm ready.
Alright, what do you call two shy people falling in love over dessert? A sweet beginning.
That's actually kind of adorable. Goodnight, chef.
Goodnight, Emily. Dream sweet, maybe of Paris rooftops and stolen chef hats.
Hey Emily! Just finished prepping tomorrow's menu, a little late-night creative spree. How's your evening treating you?
Hey. I just got back from a walk. Needed to clear my head after a long day at work. Your menu sounds way more exciting than my leftover pasta.
Leftover pasta has its place, but I'd trade you a slice of my experimental lemon cake for some of your company. Was work rough today?
Not rough, just...lonely, I guess. The office is so quiet. Sometimes I wonder if anyone would notice if I swapped my chair for a plant.
I'd notice. For the record, plants don't have that quick wit you sneak into our chats. Maybe someone at work will catch on soon, but for now, I'm glad I get the best of you.
You're sweet. I wish I believed that more often.
Trust me, it's true. I'm pretty good at reading people, the kitchen teaches you to spot the one ingredient that makes everything come alive. For you, I think it's your thoughtfulness.
You say the nicest things. What keeps you so optimistic?

I guess it's partly stubbornness and partly hope. Plus, running my own place means I get to set the tone, I want my kitchen to feel like a warm corner in a sometimes cold world. That's the kind of legacy I'd want to leave behind.
That's actually really lovely. I wish more people thought about the world they'll leave behind.
If you could design the world for future generations, what would it look like for you?
I'd want people to feel safe being themselves. I spent so long feeling like I had to hide parts of me, or stay quiet. I wish everyone could be honest and kind without worrying about being judged.
That's beautiful. Imagine a world where kindness is the norm, not the exception, where even the shyest voices are heard. I think you'd inspire that just by being yourself, honestly.
You make it sound so simple. I always feel like the odd one out, especially at work.
Maybe you're just ahead of your time, a quiet visionary. I bet the world will catch up to your kind of gentle courage.
You're a bit of a dreamer, aren't you? Not that I'm complaining.
I am! I can't help it. I daydream about running a café that doubles as a safe haven, where people can recharge, share stories, maybe even start over. Maybe one day, you'll help me pick the wallpaper.
I'd be honored. I have strong opinions on wallpaper, mostly based on Pinterest boards, but still.
Perfect. We'll blend your Pinterest wisdom with my questionable taste in vintage clocks. It'll be our own little world, a place for future dreamers.
That sounds like the kind of place I wish existed when I was younger. Maybe I wouldn't have felt so out of place back then.
You're not out of place now. Not with me, at least. If I could build anything for the next generation, it'd be a world that makes people like you feel right at home.
Thank you. That means more than you know. Can I tell you something kind of embarrassing?
Of course. You can tell me anything, promise.

I used to have a huge crush on a coworker a while back. I finally thought I'd worked up the courage to talk to him, but then I overheard him mocking me behind my back in the break room. It really stuck with me, sometimes I still feel like I'm just a punchline.

Emily, I'm so sorry that happened. You didn't deserve that, nobody does. When people say hurtful things, don't let them decide your worth. Next time something like that happens, text me right away so I can tell you the truth about you.
I wish I'd known you back then. I might have believed it.
I'm here now, and I'm not going anywhere. You're strong for sharing that. Honestly, I admire your willingness to open up, even when it's hard.
It's easier with you. You make me feel seen.

That's all I want, to make you feel safe and valued. I know what it's like to doubt yourself; I had my share of setbacks before things worked out for me. Sometimes, it's the scars that make us most interesting.
You seem so confident, though. Like, you've built this life I can't even picture for myself.

It wasn't always like this. There were years of scraping by, saving up little by little, making tough choices. But it taught me that small steps matter. I think you're already braver than you realize, just for showing up every day and not letting people like that coworker define you.
Thank you. That's honestly the nicest thing anyone's said to me all week.

You deserve to hear it every day. And hey, when you're ready for a new adventure, maybe you'll let me show you my world, late-night baking, sunrise on the roof, or even just quiet mornings with great coffee.
That sounds perfect. I'm starting to believe it could happen.
I can picture us there together, laughing over burnt toast experiments or debating which playlist sets the morning mood. I'd want to make those little rituals with you.
I love that idea. It feels like something out of a movie.
Maybe we'll make our own movie, one with less drama and more happy endings. And plenty of lemon cake, of course.
Deal. As long as I get to pick the soundtrack sometimes.
It's a deal. I trust your taste. After all, you've already improved my wallpaper game.
High praise! Are your investments paying off in interior design now?

Ha, maybe! Let's just say, learning when to take a risk, and when to ask for help, pays off in surprising ways. Sometimes those little wins let me treat myself to something I've always wanted, like a new espresso machine or a weekend getaway.
That sounds amazing. I can't picture just... deciding to take a weekend trip on a whim.
Someday, I'll convince you. Maybe we'll wander a new city and sample pastries all afternoon. Or just stay in, making pancakes and laughing at our own mess.
I'd really like that. Especially the pancake part.
It's a date, then. I'll even let you flip the first one. Worst case, we have pancake-shaped abstract art.
I'm better at eating than flipping, but I'm willing to learn.
That's all I can ask. You bring the curiosity, I'll bring the recipes, and maybe a fancy spatula, if I'm showing off.
You? Show off? Never.
Only when you're watching. You inspire me to raise my game.
You're trouble. But the good kind.
The best kind, I hope. I should let you get some rest, before I tempt you with more midnight snack ideas.
Probably for the best. Thanks for tonight. You made my day a lot brighter.
Anytime, Emily. Sleep well, and remember, you're worth more than anyone else's opinion. Sweet dreams.
Night. Talk soon?
Count on it. Goodnight, future pancake artist.
Evening, Emily. I just wrapped up a crazy dinner rush, a good kind of chaos. How's your Thursday treating you?
Hey! Nothing too wild here. Just unwinding on the couch, still trying to decide if I have the energy to cook... or just order noodles again.

You deserve to treat yourself, especially after a long week. If you lived closer, I'd send over some of tonight's signature risotto. It was a hit, even got a shoutout from a local food critic. No pressure, but I'm pretty sure my risotto could change your life.
Okay, now I'm jealous. My dinner plans sound painfully boring in comparison.

You're selling yourself short. Last time you mentioned your pasta game had hidden potential. I'm sure your noodles are at least Michelin-adjacent. Plus, I'm convinced you could make microwave soup feel like a five-star meal with your sense of humor.
That's generous, but I think 'microwave soup' is my current skill level. I wish I had your confidence in the kitchen.

I wasn't always like this. My first few months running my place, I almost burned water, if that's possible. Confidence comes from a lot of mess-ups, and a few accidental fires. You'd be surprised how much you can learn when your reputation's on the line.
It's weird to picture you nervous. You always seem so... in control.

Only on the outside. Inside, I still get those moments, like before my first big review, or whenever I try something completely new. It's that little voice of doubt. But now, I just remind myself how far I've come. I see that same determination in you, by the way.
Not sure about that. I feel like I'm still trying to figure everything out.
